target_customer: Engineering teams and enterprises calling OpenAI and Anthropic models that need per-key limits, spend control and monitoring
problem: Teams using LLM APIs had no simple way to issue scoped keys with rate limits, spend limits and expiry, or to see cost per key, other than building an in-house wrapper.
business_model: Open-core: open-source gateway plus paid hosted cloud with SSO dashboard
product_category: LLM gateway and cost control (developer tools)

founders.name: Spike Lu
founders.background_notes: YC page: senior software engineer at Unity Technologies 2019 to 2022.

founders.name: Donovan So
founders.background_notes: YC page bio contains no career information.

technical_complexity.rationale: A key management proxy in Go with rate limits and usage metrics is standard backend work, with streaming proxying the main hard part.

defensibility.rationale: The launch post names building an in-house wrapper as the main alternative, and open-source gateways with the same features were easy to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Later coverage shows many LLM gateway rivals; Portkey was acquired by Palo Alto Networks and Helicone by Mintlify in 2026, but BricksAI was not acquired per any source found.

market_need_then: LLM API adoption was just starting in 2022 to 2023 and cost control was an emerging pain, as the launch post argues, but no dated customer or spend data was found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain, cost savings focused launch post

branding.community_and_virality: The open-source repo BricksLLM was discussed on GeekNews (news.hada.io) and listed on StackShare; no evidence of a larger community.

brand_strength.rationale: Many unrelated Bricks named products (bricks.sh, BrickGPT, Bricks IDE) crowd search results and no press on the brand was found.

outcome_analysis: The cause of BricksAI's inactive status is not public. A two person team shipped an open source LLM gateway and a paid cloud in 2023 into a field that quickly filled with funded rivals, but no shutdown post, GitHub archive notice or acquisition was found, so no failure factor is assigned.
notes: No company website listed in the directory (site note: none given; trybricks.ai was not fetched). The $500K convertible note rests on CB Insights alone and is dated 2022-01-01 there, before the Summer 2022 batch, so the date is probably a placeholder; recorded as 2022 only. The YC deal itself is not recorded as a round. Competitors left empty because searches returned only 2025 and 2026 comparison pages; Helicone (YC W23, HN launch about March 2023) and LiteLLM launched after the S22 batch and are not listed. The launch post is the only dated company source and gives no date beyond 'almost 3 years ago' at read time.
